rule.usage: [族] ruler n. 统治者；直尺；rule against否决;rule over统治;as a rule通常,照例；索引p416

ex.en: Because the California law applies to all boards, even where there is no history of prior discrimination, courts are likely to rule that the law violates the constitutional guarantee of "equal protection."
ex.zh: 因为加利福尼亚州的法律适用于所有的董事会，甚至适用于那些过去没有性别歧视的地方，所以法庭很有可能判决：这项法律违反了宪法保障的"平等保护"权利。

ex.en: Under the new rules, companies must publish their pay gaps every year.
ex.zh: 根据新规定，公司必须每年公布薪酬差距。

ex.en: The region was under foreign rule for almost a century.
ex.zh: 该地区处于外国统治之下近一个世纪。

ex.en: Under the former ruler, the country expanded its territory, but ordinary citizens enjoyed few political freedoms.
ex.zh: 在前一位统治者的治下，该国扩大了疆域，但普通公民几乎没有政治自由。

senses: a. 统治的；居支配地位的

ex.en: The court's ruling obliges large companies to publish their salary data or face substantial fines.
ex.zh: 法院的裁定要求大公司公布薪酬数据，否则将面临巨额罚款。

ex.en: Shares in the firm fell sharply after a rumour spread that it had lost its largest client.
ex.zh: 一则该公司失去最大客户的传言散开后，其股价大幅下挫。

ex.en: The minister denied the rumour that he intended to resign, but few political journalists believed him.
ex.zh: 这位部长否认了打算辞职的传闻，但几乎没有政治记者相信他的话。

run.usage: [族] runner n. 跑步者；[族] runway n. 跑道

ex.en: His family has run a bakery on this street for three generations, surviving recessions and changing tastes.
ex.zh: 他家三代人都在这条街上经营一家面包店，历经经济衰退和口味的变迁。

senses: adj. 迅猛发展而难以控制的；逃跑的

ex.en: The runaway growth of online shopping has emptied many small-town high streets of their independent shops.
ex.zh: 网购的失控式增长使许多小镇商业街的独立店铺纷纷消失。

ex.en: Even a short strike at the port can disrupt supply chains that stretch across half a dozen countries.
ex.zh: 港口哪怕一场短暂的罢工也可能扰乱横跨六个国家的供应链。

rural.usage: [反] urban adj. 城市的；adj.农村的，乡村的；发音类似“孺弱”→年轻力壮的都出去打工了，农村只剩下老弱妇孺→乡下的，农村的。；索引p416

ex.en: There is no denying the limited land can no longer produce enough crops for an ever-increasing rural population.
ex.zh: 不可否认，有限的土地不能再为不断增加的农村人口生产足够的粮食。

ex.en: Young people continue to leave rural communities in search of better schools and higher wages.
ex.zh: 年轻人不断离开农村社区，去寻找更好的学校和更高的工资。

ex.en: Broadband coverage in rural England remains patchy, holding back small businesses there.
ex.zh: 英国农村的宽带覆盖仍不完善，制约了当地小企业的发展。

ex.en: Hospital staff had to rush the injured workers to the operating theatre before their conditions worsened.
ex.zh: 医护人员必须赶在伤员病情恶化前把他们火速送进手术室。

senses: a. 仓促而就的；草率的；忙碌的

ex.en: The rushed introduction of the new timetable left commuters confused and provoked a wave of complaints.
ex.zh: 仓促推行的新时刻表让通勤者一头雾水，招致一片投诉。

ex.en: Russia supplies a significant share of Europe's natural gas, a dependence that has long shaped energy policy.
ex.zh: 俄罗斯供应欧洲相当大份额的天然气，这种依赖长期左右着欧洲的能源政策。

ex.en: Leave the iron gate unpainted and it will soon show spots of rust, especially during the rainy season.
ex.zh: 铁门不刷漆很快就会出现锈斑，雨季尤甚。

ex.en: A light breeze set the dry leaves rustling, the only sound breaking the silence of the winter forest.
ex.zh: 微风拂过，枯叶沙沙作响，这是打破冬日森林寂静的唯一声响。

senses: n. 车辙,槽,凹痕;常规,老规矩

ex.en: After a decade in the same post, he felt trapped in a rut and began applying for new challenges.
ex.zh: 在同一岗位干了十年之后，他感到自己陷入了墨守成规的窠臼，开始申请新的挑战。

senses: adj. 无情的,残忍的,冷酷的

ex.en: The report portrays the chief executive as a ruthless negotiator who rarely conceded anything during the merger talks.
ex.zh: 报告把这位首席执行官描绘成冷酷无情的谈判者，在合并谈判中几乎不作让步。

ex.en: Modern farms depend heavily on costly machinery, from milking equipment to satellite-guided harvesters.
ex.zh: 现代农场严重依赖昂贵的机械设备，从挤奶设备到卫星导航收割机不一而足。

senses: n. 麻袋,纸袋,塑料袋;[the ~][口]开除,解雇

ex.en: The treasurer was given the sack after the accounts failed an independent audit for the third time.
ex.zh: 账目第三次未通过独立审计后，这位财务主管被解雇了。

senses: 宗教(性)的,神圣不可侵犯的,庄严的
adj. 神圣的，庄严的；受尊重的

phrases.m: (贬义)貌似神圣不可冒犯的人或物

sacred.usage: sacr(神圣)+-ed→神圣的；[反] secular 世俗的；[记] sacr（神圣的）+-ed（形容词后缀）。[族] sacredness n. 神圣。[近] holy a. 神圣的；同义:holy,divine;反义:secular 现世的,世俗的；发音类似“seek（寻找）red（红色）”→党组织在心中是神圣

ex.en: Human life must always be sacred.
ex.zh: 人的生命在任何时候都必须得到尊重。

ex.en: Cows are considered sacred in Hindu culture.
ex.zh: 在印度教文化中，牛被视为神圣的。

ex.en: He regarded the freedom of the press as a sacred principle.
ex.zh: 他把新闻自由视为神圣的原则。

ex.en: For the local community, the sacredness of the ancient grove forbids hunting or the felling of trees.
ex.zh: 对当地社区而言，这片古圣林的神圣性禁止狩猎或砍伐树木。

sacrifice.usage: sacr(神圣)+i+fic(做)+e→为神圣的目的做事→献祭→牺牲；[族]sacrificial a. 献祭的；sacr（神圣）+i+fice（做）→做神圣的事→献祭；sacri（神圣）+fic（做，制作）+e→做神圣的事→古时候祭祀是很神圣的事，都需要一些“献祭品”→祭品；牺牲。

ex.en: Her parents made great sacrifices to send her to university.
ex.zh: 她的父母为送她上大学做出了巨大牺牲。

ex.en: He refused to sacrifice his principles for the sake of promotion.
ex.zh: 他拒绝为了升职而牺牲自己的原则。

ex.en: Winning a championship often requires the sacrifice of personal time and comfort.
ex.zh: 赢得冠军往往需要牺牲个人时间和舒适。

senses: a. 悲哀的；令人难过的
a. 悲哀的；难过的；令人悲哀的；状况不佳的

ex.en: It is sad that so many historic buildings were demolished before anyone recognized their cultural value.
ex.zh: 令人难过的是，许多历史建筑在被拆除时无人认识到它们的文化价值。

phrases.m: 骑着马;(比喻)处于控制地位

ex.en: Experienced cyclists adjust the height of the saddle carefully, since a poor fit causes knee pain on long rides.
ex.zh: 有经验的骑手会仔细调整车座高度，因为座高不合适会导致长途骑行时膝盖疼痛。

senses: adj. 平安的；未受伤害的
a. 安全的；平安无事的；没有风险的
safe.usage: [族] safety n. 安全（链接P227）；[族] safely adv. 安全地；索引p416

ex.en: Officials assured the public that the water was safe to drink.
ex.zh: 官员们向公众保证饮用水是安全的。

ex.en: The children were finally safe after rescuers reached the flooded village.
ex.zh: 救援人员抵达被淹村庄后，孩子们终于安全了。

ex.en: She kept her savings in a safe behind the picture.
ex.zh: 她把积蓄存在画后面的保险箱里。

senses: n. 防护措施，安全措施(c)
safeguard.usage: shield 的近义词；n.保障条款，保护措施 v.保护，护卫；组合词:safe(安全)+guard(警卫)→警卫保护安全→保护，捍卫；索引p416

ex.en: Local officials are using the levers that are available to them to safeguard residents' health in the face of a serious threat.
ex.zh: 面对严重威胁，地方官员们正在使用一切可用的手段来保护居民的健康。

ex.en: New laws were introduced to safeguard consumers from false advertising.
ex.zh: 颁布新法律是为了保护消费者免受虚假广告之害。

ex.en: Strong passwords are a basic safeguard against online theft.
ex.zh: 高强度密码是防范网络盗窃的基本保护措施。

senses: n. [U] 安全；平安；安全性；安全处所
n. 安全，保险；安全性；安全场所(u)

ex.en: The new cars are tested rigorously for safety before going on sale.
ex.zh: 新车在上市前都要经过严格的安全测试。

ex.en: Workers have the right to refuse tasks that put their safety at risk.
ex.zh: 工人有权拒绝危及其安全的任务。

ex.en: The guide's first concern was the safety of the climbing party.
ex.zh: 向导首先关心的是登山队的安全。

senses: n. 圣人;智者;贤人;鼠尾草

ex.en: Villagers regarded the old teacher as a sage whose counsel was sought on every important decision.
ex.zh: 村民们把这位老教师视为智者，每逢重大决定都要向他求教。

sail.usage: [族] sailor n. 水手；[族] sailing n. 帆船运动；助记:这次sail(航行)为了递送mail(邮件);派生sailing n.航行术；启航

ex.en: They plan to sail around the world in a small boat, testing navigation equipment designed for extreme conditions.
ex.zh: 他们计划驾小船环球航行，测试为极端环境设计的导航设备。

sailor.usage: sail(航行)+or(名词后缀表示人)→海员;a bad sailor易晕船的人

ex.en: The old sailor could predict a storm from the colour of the sky long before modern instruments confirmed it.
ex.zh: 这位老水手早在现代仪器证实之前，就能凭天空的颜色预报风暴。

senses: n. (Saint略作St.用于人或地名前)圣
saint.usage: sanc(神圣)的变体；[族] saintly a. 圣洁的；派生sainted adj.神圣的,被视为圣人的

ex.en: Villagers still tell stories of the saint who, according to legend, cured the sick with water from a nearby spring.
ex.zh: 村民们仍在讲述那位圣徒的故事：传说他用附近泉水治愈了病人。

senses: a. 圣洁的；品德高尚的

ex.en: Her saintly patience with frightened patients made her the most trusted nurse in the entire hospital.
ex.zh: 她对惊恐的病人怀有圣者般的耐心，这使她成为全院最受信赖的护士。

senses: n. （for sth.'s sake）为某事本身的缘故

ex.en: He gave up smoking for the sake of his health.
ex.zh: 为了健康，他戒了烟。

ex.en: For the sake of the children, they decided not to move house during the exams.
ex.zh: 为了孩子们着想，他们决定在考试期间不搬家。

ex.en: The museum should be preserved for its own sake, not merely for tourism.
ex.zh: 博物馆应当为其自身价值而保存，而不仅仅是为了旅游。

senses: n. 色拉,(一盘)凉拌生菜

ex.en: Nutritionists recommend a fresh salad before the main course, since it increases fibre intake and reduces overall appetite.
ex.zh: 营养学家建议正餐前先吃一份新鲜色拉，因为这能增加纤维摄入并降低总体食欲。

salary.usage: [辨] salary 月薪/年薪；wage 周薪（时薪）

ex.en: The survey found that graduates in finance start on a far higher salary than those entering public service.
ex.zh: 调查发现，金融专业毕业生的起薪远高于进入公共部门的毕业生。

sale.usage: [族] salesperson n. 售货员；n.出售，销售；大减价；索引p416

ex.en: The sales for our May Books of the Month surpassed any month since 2018.
ex.zh: 5月热门图书的销量超过了自2018年以来任何月份的。

ex.en: The sale of the old factory raised funds for the new project.
ex.zh: 出售旧工厂为新项目筹集了资金。

ex.en: The store's winter sale starts next Monday.
ex.zh: 这家商店的冬季大减价下周一开始。

ex.en: A skilled salesperson devotes more attention to what the customer actually needs than to pushing the priciest model.
ex.zh: 熟练的销售员更关注顾客的真实需求，而不是一味推销最贵的型号。

senses: adj. 重要的;显著的;突出的

ex.en: The most salient finding of the survey is that support for the reform rises sharply with education level.
ex.zh: 这项调查最突出的发现是：对改革的支持度随教育水平的提高而急剧上升。

ex.en: The nurse cleaned the wound with saline before applying a fresh bandage to prevent infection.
ex.zh: 护士先用盐水清洗伤口，再换上新绷带以防感染。

ex.en: The hotel's panelled saloon served as a meeting place for travelling merchants and local landowners.
ex.zh: 旅馆里装有护墙板的客厅是往来商贩与当地地主的聚会之所。

ex.en: Doctors advise patients with high blood pressure to reduce the amount of salt in their daily diet.
ex.zh: 医生建议高血压患者减少日常饮食中的盐摄入量。

ex.en: Health campaigns urge consumers to eat less salty food, citing the links to high blood pressure.
ex.zh: 健康宣传活动劝告消费者少吃咸食，并列举了其与高血压的关联。

senses: v. 敬礼,致敬；祝贺；迎接,欢迎
n. 敬礼,祝贺；迎接,欢迎
salute.usage: 辨析:greet见面打招呼;salute正式敬礼、鸣礼炮、升旗等;hail从远处招呼;wave挥动手臂示意

ex.en: The soldiers stood straight and saluted as the national flag was raised at dawn.
ex.zh: 黎明国旗升起时，士兵们立正敬礼。

ex.en: Divers worked against the approaching winter storms to salvage cargo from the wreck lying off the coast.
ex.zh: 潜水员们赶在冬季风暴来临前，打捞沉没在近海的失事船只上的货物。

senses: n. 避免损失,躲避灾难等的途径或方法

ex.en: For struggling hill farms, tourism has become their salvation, bringing income that sheep alone no longer provide.
ex.zh: 对举步维艰的山区农场而言，旅游业成了它们的救星，带来了单靠养羊已无法提供的收入。

senses: a. 同一的；相同的；一模一样的

ex.en: The two laboratories reached the same conclusion independently, which greatly strengthened the credibility of the findings.
ex.zh: 两个实验室独立得出了相同结论，这大大增强了研究结果的可信度。

sample.usage: [近] specimen n. 样本；标本；ample(丰富的)sample(样品)；抽查这批苹果apple的样品sample

ex.en: Typically, they survey and sample large areas of terrain.
ex.zh: 通常，他们会对大面积区域进行勘测和抽样检验。

ex.en: The laboratory tests a random sample of milk from every farm each month.
ex.zh: 实验室每月对来自每个农场的牛奶进行随机抽样检测。

ex.en: Shoppers were invited to sample the new cheese free of charge.
ex.zh: 顾客被邀请免费品尝新推出的奶酪。

ex.en: The island is a wildlife sanctuary, and landing is strictly forbidden during the seabird breeding season.
ex.zh: 这座岛是野生动物保护区，海鸟繁殖季节严禁登岛。

ex.en: Trade sanctions were imposed against any country that refused to sign the agreement.
ex.zh: 凡拒签该协议的国家均受到贸易制裁。

ex.en: The UN approved economic sanctions against the country.
ex.zh: 联合国批准了对该国的经济制裁。

ex.en: Regulators sanctioned the bank for misleading customers.
ex.zh: 监管机构处罚了误导客户的银行。

ex.en: The wind carried fine sand across the highway, reducing visibility to less than fifty metres.
ex.zh: 风把细沙刮过公路，使能见度降到不足五十米。

ex.en: She grabbed a sandwich from the canteen and ate it at her desk while reviewing the survey data.
ex.zh: 她从食堂拿了块三明治，一边在办公桌前查看调查数据一边吃了起来。

senses: adj. 心智健全的,神志正常的

ex.en: No sane investor would commit all savings to a single venture that has never been tested.
ex.zh: 任何头脑清醒的投资者都不会把全部积蓄投入一个从未经过检验的项目。

senses: adj. 讽刺的,嘲笑的,挖苦的
adj. 挖苦的；尖刻的；辛辣的
sarcastic.usage: 派生sarcasm n. 讥讽,挖苦;sarcastically adv. 讥讽地；索引p416

ex.en: His sarcastic remarks about the plan offended several senior colleagues who had helped to draft it.
ex.zh: 他对该计划的挖苦评论冒犯了几位曾参与起草的高级同事。

ex.en: The reading room stays open late on Saturday, giving students a few extra hours to prepare for exams.
ex.zh: 阅览室周六延长开放，让学生们多了几个小时备考。

ex.en: Satellite images indicate that the storm is moving towards the coast faster than forecasters expected.
ex.zh: 卫星图像显示，风暴正以比预报员预期更快的速度向海岸移动。

satire.usage: 派生satirical adj.含有讽刺的,嘲弄的；发音类似“啥，累了（tire）”→才学一会就累了→“讽刺”你；索引p416

ex.en: The movie is a brilliant satire on Hollywood.
ex.zh: 这部影片是对好莱坞的绝妙讽刺。

ex.en: Political satire flourished in the newspapers of the late eighteenth century.
ex.zh: 政治讽刺作品在18世纪末的报纸上盛行。

ex.en: The novel uses gentle satire to expose the vanity of academic life.
ex.zh: 这部小说用温和的讽刺揭露了学术生活的虚荣。

senses: adj. 好讽刺的，爱挖苦人的

ex.en: His laugh was satirical, which made me feel outraged.
ex.zh: 他的笑声是讽刺的，这使我感到愤怒。

ex.en: Cartoonists have long satirised public figures, exaggerating their mannerisms to expose empty promises and hidden motives.
ex.zh: 漫画家长期讽刺公众人物，夸大其举止习惯，以揭露空洞的承诺和隐藏的动机。

senses: n. 讽刺作家；爱挖苦的人

ex.en: The satirist's weekly column was so cutting that several ministers refused all interviews with the paper.
ex.zh: 这位讽刺作家的每周专栏言辞辛辣，以致好几位部长一概拒绝接受该报采访。

ex.en: Teachers warn that a pass mark does not guarantee a satisfactory grasp of the subject.
ex.zh: 老师们警告说，及格分数并不保证对这门学科有令人满意的掌握。

senses: n. 满足，满意；令人满意的事

ex.en: She expressed her satisfaction with the team's performance.
ex.zh: 她对团队的表现表示满意。

ex.en: Customer satisfaction is the company's top priority.
ex.zh: 顾客满意是公司的头等大事。

ex.en: He looked at the finished painting with great satisfaction.
ex.zh: 他满怀满意地端详着完成的画作。

senses: adj. 令人满意的；符合要求的；良好的
adj. 令人满意的,可喜的,恰当的

ex.en: His scholastic status was perfectly satisfactory.
ex.zh: 他的学业状况十分令人满意。

ex.en: Childless folks are less likely to be satisfied with their life.
ex.zh: 没有孩子的人不太可能对自己的生活感到满意。

satisfy.usage: [族] satisfaction n. 满意；[族] satisfying adj. 令人满意的；索引p416

ex.en: The explanation failed to satisfy the committee, which ordered a fresh inquiry.
ex.zh: 这一解释未能使委员会满意，委员会下令重新调查。

ex.en: Solar panels can satisfy most of the building's energy needs.
ex.zh: 太阳能电池板可以满足该建筑的大部分能源需求。

ex.en: Nothing he did ever seemed to satisfy his demanding parents.
ex.zh: 无论他做什么，似乎都无法满足苛刻的父母。

senses: vt. 使饱和,浸透,使充满

phrases.m: 使大量吸收或充满某物

saturate.usage: satur(充足)+ate(使……)→使充满;派生saturated adj.极湿的;saturation n.浸湿,饱和；索引p416

ex.en: The market for smartphones is almost completely saturated.
ex.zh: 智能手机市场几乎已经完全饱和。

ex.en: The heavy rain saturated the ground, and the match was cancelled.
ex.zh: 大雨浸透了地面，比赛取消了。

ex.en: Consumers are saturated with advertising on every screen they look at.
ex.zh: 消费者被屏幕上铺天盖地的广告所淹没。

ex.en: The library extends its opening hours on Saturday to serve readers who work on weekdays.
ex.zh: 图书馆延长了周六的开放时间，以方便工作日上班的读者。

sauce.usage: 派生saucy adj.无礼的,莽撞的

ex.en: The chef refused to reveal the recipe for the sauce that made the restaurant famous.
ex.zh: 主厨拒绝透露让这家餐馆声名远扬的调味汁配方。

ex.en: He placed the hot cup on a saucer to protect the polished wooden table from heat marks.
ex.zh: 他把热杯子放在茶托上，以免烫坏抛光的木桌面。

ex.en: The supermarket withdrew the sausage from its shelves after tests revealed that the labels listed the wrong ingredients.
ex.zh: 检测发现标签所列成分有误后，超市将这款香肠全部下架。

senses: adj. ①野蛮的，未开化的②凶恶的，残暴的
n. 未开化的人，野蛮人(c)
vt. ①猛烈抨击，激烈批评②(动物等)凶猛地攻击

ex.en: The audit report was a savage indictment of the ministry's handling of public funds during the crisis.
ex.zh: 这份审计报告对危机期间该部委管理公共资金的方式提出了猛烈抨击。

ex.en: Opposition newspapers savagely criticised the tax plan, calling it unfair to ordinary working families.
ex.zh: 反对派报纸猛烈抨击这项税收计划，称其对普通工薪家庭不公平。

ex.en: On the open savannah, lions depend on tall grass to conceal their approach towards grazing herds.
ex.zh: 在开阔的稀树草原上，狮子依靠高草来隐蔽自己接近食草兽群的动作。

phrases.m: 储蓄以备未来之需；未雨绸缪

save.usage: [族] saving n. 节约；存款（链接P228）；串词记忆:警察救(save)了他，保证他的安全(safety)；索引p416

ex.en: But now most colleges, save for many selective campuses, allow all undergraduates, and even graduate students, to get their low grades forgiven.
ex.zh: 但是现在多数大学，除了很多择优录取学生的学校外，仍允许所有本科生，甚至研究生，得到低分宽恕（即允许重修课程以提高分数）。

ex.en: Doctors managed to save the sight in her injured eye.
ex.zh: 医生们设法保住了她受伤眼睛的视力。

ex.en: Households that save regularly are far better placed to survive sudden income losses.
ex.zh: 定期储蓄的家庭在应对突发收入损失方面要有利得多。

ex.en: Buying food in bulk can mean significant savings for large families.
ex.zh: 大宗购买食品对大家庭来说可能意味着可观的节省。

ex.en: Many households dipped into their savings during the pandemic.
ex.zh: 疫情期间，许多家庭动用了积蓄。

ex.en: The new engine offers fuel savings of up to twenty percent.
ex.zh: 新发动机可节省多达20%的燃料。

ex.en: The carpenter used a sharp saw to cut the plank into pieces of exactly equal length.
ex.zh: 木匠用一把锋利的锯子把木板锯成长度完全相等的几段。

ex.en: Employees were given a say in the redesign of the office, and the final layout reflected their preferences.
ex.zh: 员工在办公室改造中获得了发言权，最终布局反映了他们的偏好。

ex.en: As the old saying goes, a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.
ex.zh: 正如一句老话所说，一鸟在手胜过双鸟在林。

ex.en: Maintenance workers must scale the lighthouse tower twice a year to inspect the lamp housing for storm damage.
ex.zh: 维修工人必须每年两次爬上灯塔塔身，检查灯室是否被风暴损坏。

scale.usage: [族] scale up 扩大；scale down 缩小；索引p416

ex.en: The company is testing the technology on a small scale before expanding.
ex.zh: 公司正在小规模测试这项技术，然后再进行推广。

ex.en: Unemployment has fallen on a national scale for six consecutive quarters.
ex.zh: 全国范围内的失业率已连续六个季度下降。

ex.en: The map is drawn to a scale of one centimetre to one kilometre.
ex.zh: 这张地图的比例是1厘米代表1公里。

senses: n. 细看,审视;浏览,扫描
scan.usage: 发音类似"速看"→速看→浏览；扫描

ex.en: I scanned the list quickly for my name.
ex.zh: 我很快浏览了一下名单，看有没有我的名字。

ex.en: She scanned the horizon for a glimpse of the returning ships.
ex.zh: 她眺望地平线，想看一眼归来的船队。

ex.en: Doctors scanned his brain to check for damage after the accident.
ex.zh: 事故发生后，医生对他的大脑进行了扫描以检查损伤。

senses: n. 民愤,公愤;引起公愤的举动
n. 丑行，丑闻，可耻的行为
scandal.usage: [族] scandalous adj. 可耻的；令人反感的；派生scandalize v.使某人愤慨或震惊;scandalous adj.丢脸的；把明星的丑闻(scandal)照片扫描(scan)出来转发给了媒体；索引p416

ex.en: The scandal broke in May.
ex.zh: 这桩丑闻是在五月份曝光的。

ex.en: The accounting scandal forced the chairman to resign.
ex.zh: 会计丑闻迫使董事长辞职。

ex.en: The bribery scandal dominated the headlines for weeks.
ex.zh: 这起受贿丑闻连续数周占据报纸头条。

ex.en: Airport security increasingly relies on body scanners, despite some travellers' complaints about privacy and long queues.
ex.zh: 尽管一些旅客抱怨隐私和长时间排队，机场安检还是越来越依赖人体扫描仪。

ex.en: The scar on his forearm remains a reminder of the surgery that saved his sight.
ex.zh: 他前臂上的疤痕仍让人想起那场保住他视力的手术。

senses: a. 缺乏的；不足的；稀少的
scarce.usage: [族] scarcely adv. 几乎不；简直不；[族] scarcity n. 缺乏；不足；辨析:scarce指原本常见现变得稀少,常作表语;rare指珍奇珍贵;派生scarcity n.不充足,缺乏；s（联想成“美女”）+car（车）+ce（联想成“厕所”）→美女把车开进了厕所，这是很“稀有的”事。；索引p416

ex.en: Details of the accident are scarce.
ex.zh: 事故的详细情况了解不多。

ex.en: Clean water is scarce in many parts of the world.
ex.zh: 在世界的许多地方，洁净水是稀缺的。

ex.en: Skilled workers became scarce during the construction boom.
ex.zh: 在建筑热潮期间，技术工人变得短缺。

senses: adv. 几乎不,简直没有,勉强
adv. 勉强，几乎不；(表示接连发生)刚一…就

ex.en: We scarcely ever meet.
ex.zh: 我们难得见一面。

ex.en: She had scarcely sat down when the phone rang.
ex.zh: 她刚一坐下电话就响了。

ex.en: There was scarcely any food left in the fridge.
ex.zh: 冰箱里几乎没剩下什么食物。

ex.en: Scarcity enhances the pleasure of most things for most people.
ex.zh: 对大多数人来说，稀缺性增加了大多数事物的快乐。

scare.usage: [近] frighten vt. 使惊恐；scar伤疤令人scare恐惧;同义frighten,shock,alarm;辨析:scar伤疤/scare惊吓/scarce缺乏的/scary引起惊慌的；好好照顾(care)弟弟，不要动不动吓唬(scare)他

ex.en: Constant health scares just end up with no one listening.
ex.zh: 持续不断的健康恐吓最终只会无人听信。

ex.en: The shortage of the vaccine caused a scare among elderly residents.
ex.zh: 疫苗短缺在老年人中引起了恐慌。

ex.en: The sudden noise scared the birds away from the field.
ex.zh: 突然的响声把鸟儿从田里吓飞了。

ex.en: Many passengers admitted they were scared during the turbulence, though the crew remained calm and reassuring.
ex.zh: 许多乘客承认在气流颠簸中感到害怕，不过机组人员始终保持冷静、令人安心。

ex.en: She wound a woollen scarf around her neck before stepping out into the freezing wind.
ex.zh: 出门走进刺骨寒风之前，她脖子上围了一条羊毛围巾。

ex.en: The documentary describes how quickly a computer virus can spread, which many viewers found rather scary.
ex.zh: 这部纪录片描述了计算机病毒传播速度之快，许多观众觉得相当可怕。

scatter.usage: [近] spread vt. 传播；散布；辨析:scatter使杂乱散开;disperse驱散更彻底;spread普通用语指散开传开；v.撒，播撒；（使）散开，（使） 散布在各处

ex.en: The goals of the prize-givers seem as scattered as the criticism.
ex.zh: 奖项提供者的目标似乎和（他们所受的）批评一样分散。

ex.en: The wind scattered the leaves across the lawn.
ex.zh: 风把树叶吹散在草坪上。

ex.en: The crowd scattered at the sound of the gunshot.
ex.zh: 枪声一响，人群便四散跑开。

ex.en: Farms scattered across the mountains make it expensive to provide reliable electricity and clean drinking water.
ex.zh: 农场零星散布在群山之间，这使得提供稳定电力和洁净饮用水的成本很高。

senses: n. 设想;可能发生的事,可能出现的情况
[电影、戏剧等的]剧情梗概,剧本

ex.en: In the worst-case scenario, scientists estimate that sea levels could rise by more than one metre this century.
ex.zh: 在最坏的设想下，科学家估计本世纪海平面可能上升一米以上。

scene.usage: [族] scenery n. 风景（链接P314）；[近] view n. 景色

ex.en: The building has housed some of the nation's most significant diplomats and politicians and has been the scene of many historic events.
ex.zh: 这座大楼安置了美国一些最重要的外交家和政治家，成为许多历史事件的发生地。

senses: n. [U] 风景，景色；舞台布景
scenery.usage: [记] scen（布置）+-ery（名词后缀）→按演出需要在舞台上布置的场景→舞台布景；scenery（总称风景）vs scene（一处场景）；辨析:scenery指全部景色,不可数;scene可数,指部分景色、有人和活动的场面;view为普通字眼,指视力范围内的景色；scene（景色）+ery（场所，地点）→景色，风

ex.en: The scenery is magnificent.
ex.zh: 景色壮丽。

ex.en: We stopped the car to admire the mountain scenery.
ex.zh: 我们停下车来欣赏山间景色。

ex.en: The play's scenery was designed by a local artist.
ex.zh: 这出戏的舞台布景是由当地一位艺术家设计的。

senses: n. 气味；(动物留下的)嗅迹

ex.en: The dogs followed the scent left by the missing hikers and led rescuers deep into the forest.
ex.zh: 狗循着失踪徒步者留下的气味，把救援人员带进了森林深处。

ex.en: Economists remain sceptical about forecasts that assume continuous growth without any new investment.
ex.zh: 经济学家对那些假定无须任何新投资即可持续增长的预测仍持怀疑态度。

ex.en: Voters grow sceptical of promises made in the months before an election, whichever party makes them.
ex.zh: 无论出自哪个政党，选民对选举前几个月作出的承诺都会心生怀疑。

schedule.usage: 同义 timetable；是(s)车(che)堵(du)了(le)→堵车耽误了"日程安排"；索引p416

ex.en: They have a very flexible work schedule.
ex.zh: 他们的工作日程非常灵活。

ex.en: At any given point, I should have deep work scheduled for roughly the next month.
ex.zh: 在任何时候，我都应将未来约一个月时间的深度工作安排好。

ex.en: The launch is scheduled for early October, weather permitting.
ex.zh: 发射定于十月初进行，视天气情况而定。

senses: v. ①计划，策划 ②搞阴谋
n. ①计划，方案 ②阴谋，诡计
n. 计划，方案；体系，体制；阴谋
scheme.usage: 辨析：design 详尽完善；plot 各部分区分清晰；project 规模较大；scheme 对细节系统排列；s(曲线美女)+che(车)+me(我)→爱上美女，"计划"送她一辆车；索引p416

ex.en: In the grand scheme of life, one lecture really doesn't matter.
ex.zh: 在宏大的生命长卷里，一堂课真的不算什么。

ex.en: In order to "change lives for the better" and reduce "dependency," George Osborne, Chancellor of the Exchequer, introduced the "upfront work search" scheme.
ex.zh: 为了“让生活更美好”，同时降低“依赖性”，财政大臣乔治·奥斯本提出了“求职先于补助”计划。

ex.en: The government has launched a scheme to help young people find jobs.
ex.zh: 政府启动了一项帮助年轻人找工作的计划。

ex.en: The schism within the party widened after moderates were excluded from the committee drafting the programme.
ex.zh: 温和派被排除出纲领起草委员会后，党内的分裂进一步扩大。

ex.en: She won a scholarship that covered both tuition fees and living expenses for three full years.
ex.zh: 她赢得了一份奖学金，整整三年的学费和生活费都有了着落。

senses: n. 学者；奖学金获得者
scholar.usage: [族] scholarship n. 奖学金；学问（链接P228）；派生scholarly adj.博学的,好学的；schol（联想成 school“学校”）+ar（表示“人”的名词后缀）→学习的人，钻研学术的人→学者。；索引p416

ex.en: The prize attracts thousands of scholars and researchers.
ex.zh: 这个奖项吸引了成千上万的学者和研究人员。

ex.en: The visiting scholar spent a year collecting folk stories from villages along the border.
ex.zh: 这位访问学者花了一年时间收集边境沿线村庄的民间故事。

ex.en: Modern scholars question whether the manuscript was really written in the twelfth century.
ex.zh: 现代学者质疑这份手稿是否真的写于十二世纪。

senses: a. 勤奋好学的；有学问的；学术性的
adj. （书、文章、问题、活动等）学术性的；博学的
scholarly.usage: adj.学术的，勤奋好学的；索引p416

ex.en: His scholarly reputation rests on a study of medieval trade.
ex.zh: 他的学术声誉建立在一项关于中世纪贸易的研究上。

ex.en: The article appeared in a scholarly journal rather than a popular magazine.
ex.zh: 这篇文章发表在学术期刊上，而不是通俗杂志上。

ex.en: She has a scholarly interest in ancient manuscripts.
ex.zh: 她对古代手稿有着学者式的兴趣。

ex.en: She won a scholarship to study at Stanford.
ex.zh: 她获得了奖学金，得以在斯坦福大学求学。

ex.en: She won a scholarship that covered her tuition and living expenses for four years.
ex.zh: 她获得了涵盖四年学费和生活费的奖学金。

ex.en: His scholarship on ancient trade routes is admired even by researchers who disagree with him.
ex.zh: 他在古代商路方面的学术造诣，即使是与他观点相左的研究者也颇为钦佩。

senses: adj. 学校的;学业的;学术的
adj. 学术的；学校的；学者的

ex.en: Her scholastic achievements earned her a place at one of the country's leading universities.
ex.zh: 她的学业成绩为她赢得了国内一所顶尖大学的入学资格。

ex.en: The report recommends that every school provide at least one hour of physical exercise each day.
ex.zh: 报告建议每所学校每天提供至少一小时的体育锻炼。

ex.en: Children in remote districts typically receive less schooling than the national average, widening later income gaps.
ex.zh: 偏远地区的孩子接受的学校教育通常低于全国平均水平，从而拉大了日后的收入差距。

ex.en: Public confidence in science rests on honest reporting of results, including experiments that fail.
ex.zh: 公众对科学的信任有赖于对研究结果——包括失败的实验——的诚实报告。

senses: n. 科学，学科，自然科学(c/u)
n. 科学；（尤指人文、社会）学科；科学研究
science.usage: [族] scientist n. 科学家；[族] scientific adj. 科学的；索引p416

ex.en: According to the World Social Science Report 2010, the number of social-science students worldwide has swollen by about 11% every year since 2000.
ex.zh: 根据《2010年世界社会科学报告》，自2000年开始，世界各地社会科学专业的学生数量约以每年11%的速度递增。

ex.en: Good science depends on results that other researchers can verify.
ex.zh: 好的科学依赖于其他研究人员可以验证的结果。

ex.en: She chose science subjects because she enjoyed experiments and problem-solving.
ex.zh: 她选择理科，因为她喜欢实验和解题。

senses: adj. 科学的，关于科学的；细致严谨的

ex.en: In the idealized version of how science is done, facts about the world are waiting to be observed and collected by objective researchers who use the scientific method to carry out their work.
ex.zh: 在科学研究的理想状态下，客观的研究者们将运用严谨的方法开展工作，观察和收集关于世界的事实。

ex.en: There is no scientific evidence to support the claim that the vaccine causes autism.
ex.zh: 没有科学证据支持疫苗会导致自闭症的说法。

ex.en: The expedition gathered scientific data on the melting of the ice sheet.
ex.zh: 探险队收集了关于冰盖融化的科学数据。

ex.en: The scientist spent decades studying the behaviour of glaciers.
ex.zh: 这位科学家花了数十年研究冰川的活动。

ex.en: Many scientists warned that the drug had been tested on too small a sample.
ex.zh: 许多科学家警告说，这种药物的试验样本太小。

ex.en: Data scientists are now among the most sought-after employees in finance.
ex.zh: 数据科学家目前是金融业最抢手的员工之一。

ex.en: The assembly instructions advise cutting along the marked line with a pair of sharp scissors.
ex.zh: 组装说明建议用一把锋利的剪刀沿标出的线剪开。

scold.usage: 酒店太冷(cold)，他们忍不住跑到前台训斥(scold)酒店经理；索引p416

ex.en: He scolded them for arriving late.
ex.zh: 他嫌他们迟到，训了他们一通。

ex.en: The mother scolded her son for breaking the window.
ex.zh: 母亲因儿子打破窗户而责骂他。

ex.en: Employees were scolded for arriving late to the meeting.
ex.zh: 员工们因开会迟到而受到训斥。

senses: n. 铲;勺,勺状物;一勺(之量);独家新闻
v. 舀,盛;铲;抢先报道;获取,赢得;抱起,拿起

ex.en: The young journalist's scoop about the missing funds forced the ministry to answer questions in parliament.
ex.zh: 这位年轻记者关于资金失踪的独家报道迫使该部委在议会上接受质询。

ex.en: Even a modest telescope reveals the rings of Saturn clearly on a cold, cloudless night.
ex.zh: 在寒冷无云的夜晚，即使一台普通望远镜也能清晰地看到土星的光环。

scope.usage: 很多时只能解决(cope)能力范围(scope)内的问题；索引p416

ex.en: There's still plenty of scope for improvement.
ex.zh: 还有很大的改进余地。

ex.en: The inquiry's scope was limited to the years after 2010, which critics said ignored earlier warnings.
ex.zh: 调查范围仅限于2010年之后，批评者称这忽视了更早的预警。

ex.en: There is little scope for negotiation once the contract has been signed by both parties.
ex.zh: 合同一经双方签署，几乎没有谈判的余地。

ex.en: Applicants with a score above ninety percent are excused from the second round of written tests.
ex.zh: 得分超过百分之九十的申请者可免于第二轮笔试。

scorn.usage: 不应该鄙视(scorn)种玉米(corn)的农民；索引p416

ex.en: Homework has never been terribly popular with students and even many parents, but in recent years it has been particularly scorned.
ex.zh: 家庭作业从来就没有受到学生甚至许多家长的特别欢迎，而近年来更是备受贬损。

ex.en: She poured scorn on the claim that the drug was completely safe.
ex.zh: 她对那种药物完全安全的说法嗤之以鼻。

ex.en: He scorned the offer of help and insisted on doing it alone.
ex.zh: 他蔑视别人提供的帮助，坚持独自完成。

ex.en: Senior academics were scornful of the theory at first, but later field studies compelled them to reconsider.
ex.zh: 资深学者起初对这一理论不屑一顾，但后来的实地研究迫使他们重新审视。

scotland.usage: adj. Scottish；人 Scot (Scotsman, Scotswoman); the Scots

ex.en: Scotland now generates most of its electricity from wind and exports surplus power to its southern neighbours.
ex.zh: 苏格兰如今的电力大部分来自风能，并将富余电力输送给南面的邻区。

ex.en: The club sent a scout to watch the young striker in three matches before offering him a contract.
ex.zh: 俱乐部在向这名年轻前锋提供合同之前，派了一名球探观看了他的三场比赛。

senses: v. 攀登;(蔓草等)蔓延,繁生;(for)争夺,竞争;搅乱
n. 攀登,爬行;争夺,抢夺

ex.en: Survivors had to scramble up the steep hillside to reach the road and flag down passing cars.
ex.zh: 幸存者不得不攀上陡峭的山坡到达公路，拦下过路汽车。

senses: n. 碎片,零屑;少量,一点儿;废料,废物
vt. 抛弃；把…报废；使解体

ex.en: The government decided to scrap the outdated tax scheme after businesses complained about its complexity.
ex.zh: 在企业抱怨旧税制过于复杂后，政府决定将其废除。

senses: v. 用程序从网上下载（数据）；刮，擦
scrape.usage: 辨析:scrape刮擦;scratch用爪刨抓;scrap名词碎片;slit切开撕开；索引p416

ex.en: The researchers wrote a simple program to scrape data from hundreds of publicly available web pages.
ex.zh: 研究人员编写了一个简单程序，从数百个公开网页上抓取数据。

senses: v. 抓,搔,刮,擦;潦草地涂画,乱画
scratch.usage: 同义scrape,rub；sc(谐音“四个”)+rat(老鼠)+ch(谐音“吃”)→四个老鼠偷吃粮食，把谷仓外边“抓”出很多“划痕”

ex.en: The company built its first laboratory from scratch in an old warehouse.
ex.zh: 公司在一个旧仓库里从零开始建起了第一个实验室。

ex.en: Be careful—that cat will scratch if you pick it up.
ex.zh: 小心——你一抱那只猫，它就会抓人。

ex.en: He scratched his name on the bench with a knife.
ex.zh: 他用小刀在长凳上刻下自己的名字。

senses: v. 尖叫，高声喊，大声叫
scream.usage: [辨] scream 尖叫；[近] yell 喊叫；shriek 尖声叫；她看见cream(奶油)撒在地上就scream(尖声叫)起来；同事们把奶油(cream)抹到她脸上，她激动地尖叫(scream)起来

ex.en: The kids were screaming with excitement.
ex.zh: 孩子们兴奋地叫喊着。

ex.en: She screamed for help when she saw smoke coming from the kitchen.
ex.zh: 看到厨房冒烟时，她大声呼救。

ex.en: The tabloids screamed about the scandal for weeks.
ex.zh: 数周来，小报都在大肆叫嚷这桩丑闻。

ex.en: With so much focus on children's use of screens, it's easy for parents to forget about their own screen use.
ex.zh: 随着儿童对屏幕（数字产品）的使用备受关注，父母很容易忽视他们自己对屏幕（数字产品）的使用。

ex.en: All newborns are screened for hearing problems shortly after birth.
ex.zh: 所有新生儿出生后不久都要接受听力问题筛查。

ex.en: The ceremony will be screened live to millions of viewers around the world.
ex.zh: 典礼将向全球数百万观众现场直播。

screw.usage: crew(全体船员)都拿着screw(螺丝)；发音类似“四个懦（生）”→想象四个文弱书生在那拧“螺丝钉”，累得满头大汗也没“固定”住→用螺丝钉固定。

ex.en: A screw is stronger than a nail.
ex.zh: 螺丝钉比普通钉子牢固。

ex.en: He screwed the shelf to the wall before putting any books on it.
ex.zh: 他先把架子拧到墙上，然后再放书。

ex.en: One loose screw made the whole machine rattle.
ex.zh: 一颗松动的螺丝使整台机器咔嗒作响。

senses: n. 手稿,考生的笔试卷
script.usage: [族] scriptwriter n. 编剧；[族] describe/description 源自 script（链接P231）；scrip（写）+t→写的东西→笔迹；剧本

ex.en: He was reading from a prepared script.
ex.zh: 他在读一份准备好的剧本。

ex.en: The actors complained that the script needed rewriting before filming began.
ex.zh: 演员们抱怨说，开拍前剧本需要重写。

ex.en: Cuneiform was among the earliest scripts used to record trade in Mesopotamia.
ex.zh: 楔形文字是最早用于记录美索不达米亚贸易的文字之一。

senses: v. 擦洗,擦净;删除;取消
n. 灌木丛(地带);刷洗,擦洗;磨砂(膏);医院工作服(scrubs)

ex.en: Volunteers spent the morning scrubbing graffiti off the subway walls before the morning rush began.
ex.zh: 志愿者们趁早高峰来临前花了一上午擦洗地铁墙壁上的涂鸦。

ex.en: Public spending on the project will come under close scrutiny by an independent audit office.
ex.zh: 该项目的公共开支将受到独立审计机构的严格审查。

ex.en: Further arrangements—and there may be many—between the NHS and DeepMind will be carefully scrutinized to ensure that all necessary permissions have been asked of patients and all unnecessary data has been cleaned.
ex.zh: 国民健康服务基金会(NHS)和深度思想之间的进一步的协议——可能非常多——将会受到严格审核，以确保都已征得了病患的所有必要的许可并清除了所有不必要的数据。

ex.en: Parliamentary committees scrutinise every clause of a new bill before it is allowed to proceed further.
ex.zh: 议会委员会在新法案获准继续推进之前，会逐条加以仔细审查。

senses: vt. 仔细检查，认真查看，详审

ex.en: Regulators now scrutinize every large merger to ensure that consumers will not face higher prices.
ex.zh: 监管机构现在会仔细审查每一笔大型合并，以确保消费者不会面临更高的价格。

senses: n. 详细审查;细看,监视
n. 仔细检查，认真彻底的审查
scrutiny.usage: 复数 scrutinies。近义：examination n. 审查；[族] scrutinize vt. 仔细检查；派生scrutinize v.仔细或彻底检查；多小的（tiny）错误我们都要仔细检查（scrutiny）。；索引p416

ex.en: Manuscript will be flagged up for additional scrutiny by the journal's internal editors, or by its existing Board of Reviewing Editors or by outside peer reviewers.
ex.zh: 原稿将由该期刊的内部编辑、其现有评审编委会或外部同行评审者作出标记，以接受额外审查。

ex.en: The company's accounting practices have come under close scrutiny since the fraud was exposed.
ex.zh: 自舞弊行为曝光以来，该公司的会计做法一直受到严格审查。

ex.en: Every new drug must survive years of scientific scrutiny before it can be sold to patients.
ex.zh: 每一种新药都必须经受多年的科学审查，才能出售给患者。

senses: n. 雕刻,雕刻品,雕塑,雕塑品
sculpture.usage: [族] sculptor n. 雕塑家；派生sculptural adj.雕塑的;sculptor n.雕塑家；索引p416

ex.en: The garden features a large bronze sculpture of a dancing couple.
ex.zh: 花园里有一座双人起舞的大型青铜雕塑。

ex.en: She studied sculpture in Florence before turning to painting.
ex.zh: 她在佛罗伦萨学习雕塑，后来转向绘画。

ex.en: Ice sculptures attract thousands of visitors to the winter festival.
ex.zh: 冰雕吸引着成千上万的游客来到这个冬季节日。

ex.en: Half the village earns its living from the sea, catching fish or ferrying tourists between the islands.
ex.zh: 村里一半的人靠海谋生，或捕鱼，或在岛屿间摆渡游客。

ex.en: Seagulls have moved into city centres, scavenging from bins as fishing ports no longer feed them.
ex.zh: 海鸥已进入市中心，由于渔港不再给它们提供食物，它们便在垃圾箱里觅食。

senses: n. 海豹(c);封铅,封条(c);印,图章(c)

ex.en: The treaty was signed and sealed by representatives of both governments.
ex.zh: 该条约由两国政府代表签署并盖章。

ex.en: The envelope was sealed with wax to prevent anyone reading the letter.
ex.zh: 信封用火漆封好，防止任何人偷看信件。

ex.en: Conservationists track seals in the North Sea to study fish stocks.
ex.zh: 自然保护者在北海追踪海豹，以研究鱼类资源。

seam.usage: 派生seamless adj.无缝的,无伤痕的

ex.en: The tailor inspected every seam of the wedding dress before handing it to the anxious bride.
ex.zh: 裁缝在把婚纱交到焦虑的新娘手中之前，检查了每一条接缝。

search.usage: [辨] search sb. 搜身；search for sb. 寻找某人；辨：强调搜寻具体的人或某一具体事物；索引p416

ex.en: In many such cases, a cursory search for causes finds that some small group of people was wearing, promoting, or developing whatever it is before anyone else paid attention.
ex.zh: 在诸多类似的案例中，粗略调查一下其中的原因就会发现，总有一小群人在别人注意到之前就率先穿戴、推广或开发这些东西。

ex.en: Rescuers searched the ruins for survivors throughout the night.
ex.zh: 救援人员彻夜在废墟中搜寻幸存者。

ex.en: She has been searching for a cure for the disease since her daughter was diagnosed.
ex.zh: 自女儿被确诊以来，她一直在寻找治疗这种疾病的方法。

senses: adj. 灼热的;强烈的;猛烈批评的
adj. (疼痛、热量等)强烈的；猛烈批评的

ex.en: The article offers a searing critique of the government's failure to prepare hospitals for the epidemic.
ex.zh: 文章对政府未能让医院做好疫情准备提出了猛烈的批评。

ex.en: Children wandered the shore collecting seashells, each hoping to find one with a perfect spiral.
ex.zh: 孩子们在岸边游走捡拾贝壳，每个人都盼着找到一枚螺纹完美的。

ex.en: Cheap flights abroad have drained visitors from the traditional seaside towns of the British coast.
ex.zh: 廉价的出境航班使游客远离了英国海岸传统的海滨小镇。

ex.en: Tourist numbers vary sharply with the season, peaking in July and August along the entire coast.
ex.zh: 游客数量随季节变化剧烈，整个海岸线的旅游高峰出现在七八月。

senses: a. 季节性的；随季节变化的；节令性的
adj. 季节(性)的;随季节变化的;节令性的

ex.en: The hotel relies heavily on seasonal workers, so employment in the town falls sharply after the summer months.
ex.zh: 这家旅馆严重依赖季节工，因此夏季一过镇上的就业人数便急剧下降。

senses: n. 座位,底座;所在地,场所
seat.usage: [辨] seat 及物；sit 不及物

ex.en: She held the parliamentary seat for twelve years before retiring from politics in 2019.
ex.zh: 她在2019年退出政坛前，曾拥有该议会席位长达十二年。

ex.en: Coastal farmers once gathered seaweed in quantity and spread it on their fields as fertiliser.
ex.zh: 沿海农民曾大量采集海藻，撒到田里作肥料。

ex.en: Modern cameras capture several images per second, revealing details that remain invisible to the naked eye.
ex.zh: 现代相机每秒能拍摄多幅图像，揭示出肉眼看不见的细节。

ex.en: The novelist lived in seclusion in the mountains, declining interviews and avoiding social media entirely.
ex.zh: 这位小说家隐居山中，拒绝采访，也完全不碰社交媒体。

senses: adj. 第二的;次等的,次要的

ex.en: The committee approved the proposal a second time after revising the budget figures.
ex.zh: 委员会在修订预算数字后第二次批准了该提案。

senses: a. 中学的；中等教育的
secondary.usage: [族] second num. 第二（链接P230）；[反] primary adj. 首要的；[记] second（第二）+-ary（形容词后缀）→第二位的→次要的。[近] subordinate, minor a. 次要的；second(第二)+ary(形容词后缀)→第二的

ex.en: The study suggests that cost should remain a secondary consideration when patient safety is at stake.
ex.zh: 研究表明，当患者安全受到威胁时，成本仍应作为次要考虑因素。

secret.usage: [族] secretary n. 秘书；[族] secrecy n. 保密

ex.en: The two firms signed a secret agreement to fix prices, which investigators later found in the company's archives.
ex.zh: 两家公司签署了一份秘密定价协议，调查人员后来在公司档案中发现了它。

secretary.usage: 派生secretarial adj.书记的,秘书的；n.秘书；部长，大臣；助理

ex.en: The secretary keeps the minutes of every board meeting.
ex.zh: 秘书负责记录每次董事会会议的纪要。

ex.en: She worked as a secretary in a law firm before studying for a degree.
ex.zh: 她在攻读学位之前曾在一家律师事务所当秘书。

ex.en: The Foreign Secretary will attend the summit on behalf of the Prime Minister.
ex.zh: 外交大臣将代表首相出席峰会。

section.usage: [族] sector n. 部门；行业（链接P230）；sect(切)+ion→可以切掉的→部分;派生sectionalism n.地方主义；词根记忆：sect(cut,切)+ion(名词后缀)→把东西切成几部分→部分；索引p416

ex.en: The sports section of the newspaper has been cut to save costs.
ex.zh: 报纸的体育版面被削减以节省开支。

ex.en: Only a small section of the railway remains in use today.
ex.zh: 如今这条铁路只剩一小段仍在使用。

ex.en: The final section of the book examines the consequences of the war.
ex.zh: 本书的最后一部分探讨了这场战争的后果。

sector.usage: sect（切，割）+or（名词后缀）→切开，切割→分成部分→部门。；词根记忆：sect(cut,切)+or(名词后缀)→切分管理→部门；索引p416

ex.en: China is making efforts to expand such economic sectors as tourism and information technology.
ex.zh: 中国正在努力发展旅游业和信息技术等经济部门。

ex.en: Improving living standards and increasing prosperity for more people will require greater use of digital technologies to boost productivity in various sectors, including health care and construction, says Coyle.
ex.zh: 科伊尔说，提高更多人的生活水平和促进繁荣将需要更大程度地运用数字技术来提高各行业的生产力，包括医疗保健和建筑业。

ex.en: The service sector now accounts for most jobs in advanced economies.
ex.zh: 服务业现在占发达经济体就业岗位的大多数。

senses: adj. 现世的,世俗的;非宗教的

ex.en: Modern states increasingly keep education secular, leaving religious instruction to families and private institutions.
ex.zh: 现代国家日益保持教育世俗化，把宗教教育留给家庭和私立机构。

senses: vt. （尤指经过努力）获得；取得
secure.usage: [族] security n. 安全；保障（链接P230）；[近] obtain vt. 获得；adj.稳固的，可靠的；牢固的； 安全的 v.（尤指经过努力而）获得；使 安全，保护；将（某物）固定；；adj.稳固的，可靠的；安全的 v.(经过努力)获得；保护；②vt.(尤指经过努力)获得(2020年阅读):With t

ex.en: During the past generation, the American middle-class family that once could count on hard work and fair play to keep itself financially secure has been transformed by economic risk and new realities.
ex.zh: 在上一代人中，美国中产阶级家庭曾经依靠努力工作和公平竞争来保持自己的经济安全，但现在却被经济危机和新的现实所改变。

ex.en: The career office found the most desirable trait in a future employer was the ability to offer secure employment (followed by professional development and training, and then inspiring purpose).
ex.zh: 该就业办公室发现未来雇主最令人向往的特征是能够提供有保障的就业（其次是职业发展和培训，最后是鼓舞人心的目标）。

ex.en: The young firm finally secured a contract with a major airline after two years of negotiation.
ex.zh: 经过两年的谈判，这家年轻的公司终于获得了一家大型航空公司的合同。

security.usage: n.保护措施；保安部门；安全； 抵押品；证券；索引p416

ex.en: The job security that the U.S. economy once offered to high school graduates has largely evaporated.
ex.zh: 美国经济曾为高中毕业生提供的那种（肯定能找到）工作的安全感在很大程度上已经不复存在了。

ex.en: Critics argue that the new security measures cause long queues without making passengers any safer.
ex.zh: 批评者认为，新的安检措施造成了长时间的排队，却没有让乘客更安全。

ex.en: Many graduates now prefer job security to high salaries when choosing their first employer.
ex.zh: 许多毕业生在选择第一份工作时，如今更看重工作保障而非高薪。

ex.en: The vet administered a mild sedative to the frightened horse before examining its injured leg.
ex.zh: 兽医在检查这匹受惊马的伤腿之前，先给它用了温和的镇静剂。

senses: n. [U] 煽动叛乱的言论(或行动)
n. 煽动叛乱的言论(或行为)

ex.en: The colonial authorities charged the newspaper editor with sedition after he published articles calling for independence.
ex.zh: 这位报纸主编发表呼吁独立的文章后，殖民当局以煽动叛乱罪起诉了他。

ex.en: Critics warn that glossy advertising can seduce consumers into buying goods they neither need nor can afford.
ex.zh: 批评者警告说，华丽的广告会诱使消费者购买他们既不需要也负担不起的商品。

ex.en: Economists see little evidence that the tax cuts have stimulated investment in manufacturing.
ex.zh: 经济学家几乎没有看到减税刺激制造业投资的证据。

ex.en: The agency distributes seed to farmers before the rainy season, along with advice on irrigation and soil management.
ex.zh: 该机构在雨季前向农民发放种子，并就灌溉和土壤管理提供建议。

seek.usage: [族] seeker n. 追求者；探寻者；①寻求:seek long-term prosperity ②寻找:seek a job ③请求:seek permission征得许可；辨:强调对崇高目标或抽象事物的追求向往；索引p416

ex.en: Scientists are increasingly seeking out visual artists to help them communicate their work to new audiences.
ex.zh: 越来越多的科学家正在寻求视觉艺术家来帮助他们向新的受众传播他们的工作。

ex.en: Graduates are seeking jobs that offer both income and meaning.
ex.zh: 毕业生正在寻找既有收入又有意义的工作。

ex.en: The company sought permission to expand its factory.
ex.zh: 该公司申请了扩建工厂的许可。

ex.en: The job fair attracted thousands of job seekers, many of them recent graduates with little work experience.
ex.zh: 这场招聘会吸引了数千名求职者，其中许多是缺乏工作经验的应届毕业生。

books.unit: 常见冠词、情态动词、系动词与限定词

senses: v.-link. 好像，似乎，看来；感到好像
v. (涉及推断)好像,似乎,看来
v. 感到好像,觉得似乎

ex.en: House prices in the capital seem to have stabilized after three years of continuous increases.
ex.zh: 在连续三年上涨之后，首都的房价似乎已经企稳。

senses: adv. 表面上地;在……看来,就我们所知而言

ex.en: A seemingly minor change in the law had a major effect on how small businesses kept their records.
ex.zh: 法律上一项看似微小的修改，对小企业的记账方式产生了重大影响。

ex.en: The final section of the report lists the measures the ministry intends to introduce over the next year.
ex.zh: 报告的最后一节列出了该部委打算在来年推出的各项措施。

segment.usage: [族] segmentation n. 分割；细分；n.部分，片段 v.分割，划分；词根记忆：seg(cut,切)+ment(名词后缀)→把东西切成几部分→部分；索引p416

ex.en: Big retailers must understand these differences before they can identify the segments of European wholesaling in which their particular abilities might unseat smaller but entrenched competitors.
ex.zh: 大型零售商必须了解这些差异，才能确定欧洲批发业的细分市场，从而可能利用自己独有的能力从中挤走那些规模较小但是地位稳固的竞争者。

ex.en: The firm targets the fastest-growing segment of the smartphone market.
ex.zh: 这家公司瞄准智能手机市场增长最快的部分。

ex.en: A large segment of the audience left before the film ended.
ex.zh: 很大一部分观众在电影结束前就离场了。

senses: adj. 分离的,隔开的,单独的
segregate.usage: se(分开)+greg(群体)+ate(使……)→使群体分开→隔离;派生segregation n.隔离；se(表示"分开")+greg(群体)+ate(动词后缀，使……)→使群体分开→使分开，使隔离

ex.en: Pedestrians are segregated from the traffic by a metal barrier.
ex.zh: 行人被一个金属屏障与交通隔开。

senses: vt. 夺取，攻占，控制；逮捕

ex.en: Customs officers seized a large quantity of counterfeit medicine at the port last week.
ex.zh: 海关官员上周在港口查获了大量假药。

ex.en: Researchers seldom publish negative results, a practice that some argue distorts the scientific record.
ex.zh: 研究人员很少发表阴性结果，有人认为这种做法扭曲了科学记录。

senses: ②(在计算机屏幕上、从菜单中)选定，选取
adj. ①精选的，选择的，优等的；②一流的，只为富人(或上层人士)而设的
select.usage: 辨析：select 指经过认真考虑后，仔细从中精选出最好的、最中意的；索引p416

ex.en: Through carefully selected words and phrases, poems can be dramatic, funny, beautiful, moving and inspiring.
ex.zh: 通过斟酌词句，诗歌可以是戏剧性的、滑稽有趣的、美妙迷人的、感人肺腑的，也可以是鼓舞人心的。

ex.en: A committee was formed to select the next university president.
ex.zh: 成立了一个委员会来遴选下一任大学校长。

ex.en: Only the finest grapes are selected for this wine.
ex.zh: 只有最优质的葡萄才被选用来酿造这种葡萄酒。

ex.en: The selection of a new manager will take place next month.
ex.zh: 新经理的遴选将于下个月进行。

ex.en: The shop offers a wide selection of cheeses from small farms.
ex.zh: 这家商店提供来自小农场的多种奶酪供挑选。

ex.en: Natural selection explains how species gradually adapt to their environment.
ex.zh: 自然选择解释了物种如何逐渐适应环境。

senses: adj. 选择性的；仔细挑选的

ex.en: The university is highly selective, admitting fewer than one applicant in ten for its most popular courses.
ex.zh: 这所大学选拔极为严格，最受欢迎的课程录取率不到十分之一。

ex.en: Memory tends to work selectively, preserving flattering episodes while quietly dropping the embarrassing ones.
ex.zh: 记忆往往有选择地发挥作用，保留体面的片段，悄悄抹去尴尬的往事。

senses: n. ①个性，自我，本身，自己
②(自己的)通常行为方式，本来面目，惯常心态

ex.en: Meditation teachers claim that observing the self without judgement can reduce stress and improve concentration.
ex.zh: 冥想导师声称，不加评判地观察自我可以减压并提高专注力。

senses: a. 自我中心的；只考虑自己的

ex.en: Critics argue that social media encourages young people to become self-centered, caring little about the communities in which they live.
ex.zh: 批评者认为，社交媒体促使年轻人变得自我中心，几乎不关心他们所生活的社区。

ex.en: Psychologists warn that self-deception may temporarily protect our confidence, but it ultimately prevents us from correcting our real weaknesses.
ex.zh: 心理学家警告说，自我欺骗或许能暂时保护我们的自信，但最终会妨碍我们改正真正的缺点。

senses: adj. 明摆着的，不言而喻的

ex.en: It seems self-evident that students learn better when they get enough sleep, yet few schools adjust their timetables accordingly.
ex.zh: 睡眠充足的学生学得更好，这似乎是不言而喻的，但很少有学校据此调整课程安排。

senses: n. [U] 自我表现，自我表达

ex.en: For many teenagers, painting and music are important channels of self-expression rather than merely hobbies.
ex.zh: 对许多青少年来说，绘画和音乐是自我表达的重要渠道，而不仅仅是爱好。

ex.en: The bookshop has expanded its self-help section, reflecting growing public interest in personal development.
ex.zh: 书店扩大了自助类图书区，反映出公众对个人成长的兴趣日益浓厚。

senses: n. [U] 自私自利；利己主义

ex.en: Economists have long assumed that firms are motivated mainly by self-interest, though cooperation is also widespread in business.
ex.zh: 经济学家长期假定企业主要受私利驱动，但商业领域中的合作同样普遍。

senses: adj. 利己主义的,自私的

ex.en: The proposal was attacked as a self-interested attempt by wealthy countries to protect their own industries.
ex.zh: 该提案被指责为富裕国家保护自身产业的利己企图。

ex.en: After decades of struggle, the colony finally won self-rule and began to build its own political institutions.
ex.zh: 经过数十年的斗争，该殖民地终于赢得自治，并开始建立自己的政治制度。

ex.en: Critics called the decision selfish, arguing that it protected the company's profits at the workers' expense.
ex.zh: 批评者称这一决定自私，认为它以牺牲工人利益为代价保护公司利润。

senses: v. 出让，转让；出售，售卖

ex.en: The museum cannot legally sell any of the paintings donated to it a century ago.
ex.zh: 按规定，博物馆不能合法出售一个世纪前捐赠给它的任何画作。

ex.en: The online seller promised delivery within two days, but complaints about delayed orders continued to rise.
ex.zh: 这位网上卖家承诺两天内送货，但关于订单延迟的投诉仍在不断增加。

ex.en: Words such as assemble and resemble share the root semble, which means together or like, and they appear frequently in academic texts.
ex.zh: assemble 与 resemble 等词共享词根 semble，意为“相同、一起”，它们在学术文章中经常出现。

ex.en: I was finishing my last semester in college and trying to look for a job.
ex.zh: 我当时即将结束最后一个学期的大学生活，正想找份工作。

ex.en: I spent a semester at the University of Madrid.
ex.zh: 我在马德里大学待了一个学期。

ex.en: The new course will be offered to seniors in the autumn semester.
ex.zh: 新课程将在秋季学期向毕业班学生开设。

ex.en: The global shortage of semiconductor chips forced several car factories to halt production for weeks.
ex.zh: 全球半导体芯片短缺迫使多家汽车工厂停产数周。

senses: n. 研讨课，研讨会，培训会

ex.en: Professor Mackay will give a seminar on Pound's poetry.
ex.zh: 麦凯教授将开设一个关于庞德诗歌的研讨课。

ex.en: The department runs a weekly seminar on environmental economics.
ex.zh: 该系每周举办一次环境经济学研讨课。

ex.en: She presented her research at a seminar for doctoral students.
ex.zh: 她在一个博士生研讨会上介绍了自己的研究。

ex.en: Derived from the root sen, meaning old, words such as senior and senate originally referred to the elder members of society.
ex.zh: senior 与 senate 等词源自意为“老”的词根 sen，原本指社会中的年长者。

senate.usage: 派生senatorial adj.参议院的,上院的；n.参议院；索引p416

ex.en: The bill was approved by the senate after a debate that lasted late into the night.
ex.zh: 经过一场持续到深夜的辩论后，该法案获得了参议院的批准。

ex.en: Several senators broke with their party to vote against the proposal in the senate.
ex.zh: 几位参议员违背本党立场，在参议院投票反对该提案。

ex.en: Under the constitution, the senate must confirm senior judges before they take office.
ex.zh: 根据宪法，高级法官必须经参议院确认后才能就职。

ex.en: The senator was invited but was unable to attend.
ex.zh: 参议员受到了邀请，但是未能出席。

ex.en: The senator promised to push for tighter gun controls.
ex.zh: 这位参议员承诺推动更严格的枪支管制。

ex.en: Two senators voted against the defence budget.
ex.zh: 两名参议员对国防预算投了反对票。

senses: vt. 邮寄；发送；派遣；打发；安排去
③使快速移动；使做出(某种反应)，使表现出(某种行为)

ex.en: The university will send admissions decisions by email at the end of March.
ex.zh: 大学将于三月底通过电子邮件发送录取结果。

senses: a. 年长的；地位较高的
adj. ①年长的 ②资格老的，地位较高的
senior.usage: 派生 seniority n. 年长；资历深；adj.年龄大些的;年长的； 高级的 n.较年长的人；长者；地 位较高者；sen（年老）+ior（较……的）→年长的；索引p416

ex.en: I have ten years' experience at senior management level.
ex.zh: 我有十年的高层管理经验。

ex.en: Several senior managers resigned after the report criticised the company's safety record.
ex.zh: 报告批评了该公司的安全记录后，几名高级管理人员辞职了。

ex.en: Senior citizens are entitled to discounted travel on trains and buses throughout the country.
ex.zh: 老年人有权在全国范围内享受火车和巴士的票价折扣。

ex.en: Promotion in the company depends on merit rather than seniority, which encourages younger employees to compete.
ex.zh: 该公司的晋升取决于能力而非资历，这鼓励了年轻员工展开竞争。

ex.en: Because the root sens or sent means to feel, it appears in words describing emotion and perception, such as sensible and sensitive.
ex.zh: 由于词根 sens 或 sent 意为“感觉”，它出现在描述情感与感知的词汇中，例如 sensible 和 sensitive。

senses: n. ①(身体上的)感觉，知觉(c)
n. ②感觉能力，知觉能力(u)
③激动；轰动，轰动一时的事情(c)
n. 感觉（能力），知觉（能力）；轰动
sensation.usage: 派生 sensational adj. 耸人听闻的，轰动的

ex.en: News of his arrest caused a sensation.
ex.zh: 他被捕的消息引起了轰动。

senses: adj. 引起轰动的;哗众取宠的;极好的;绝妙的
adj. 轰动的；耸人听闻的

ex.en: Their sometimes sensational findings were filled with warnings about the growing competition from overseas.
ex.zh: 有时他们那些耸人听闻的发现里充满了对海外竞争日益增长的警告之词。

senses: ②观念，意识；③判断力，鉴赏力；④见识，智慧；⑤道理，合理性；⑥意义，含义(c)
sense.usage: 另 make sense 讲得通，言之成理；sense of security安全感；make sense有意义；说得通；in one sense在某种意义上；common sense常识；索引p416

ex.en: When more and more of us have a degree, it makes sense to have two.
ex.zh: 当我们中越来越多的人拥有一个学位时，拥有两个学位是有意义的。

ex.en: But when it came to their houses, it was a time of common sense and a belief that less could truly be more.
ex.zh: 但当涉及他们的房子时，这是一个"少即是多"成为常识和信念的时代。

ex.en: CEOs must have a good sense of financial markets and maybe even how the company should trade in them.
ex.zh: 首席执行官们必须对金融市场有良好的判断，甚至可能还得判断公司应该如何在金融市场中进行交易。

senses: adj. 愚蠢的，无意义的；无知觉的

sensible.usage: sensible（明智的）vs sensitive（敏感的）；adj.理智的，合理的；实用的； 可感觉到的，明显的；索引p416

ex.en: The sensible place to build new houses, factories and offices is where people are, in cities and towns where infrastructure is in place.
ex.zh: 建造新房子、工厂和办公室的明智地点是在人多的地方，在基础设施完备的城镇。

ex.en: It is sensible to keep copies of all documents in case the originals are lost.
ex.zh: 把所有文件都留有副本是明智的，以防原件丢失。

ex.en: She took the sensible precaution of checking the weather forecast before setting out on the climb.
ex.zh: 出发登山前查看天气预报，她这一预防措施做得明智。

senses: a. 过敏的；易受影响的
adj. ①敏感的；易受伤害的；艺术感觉好的
adj. 敏感的；过敏的；体贴的；感觉敏锐的
sensitive.usage: adj.灵敏的；体恤的；敏感的；；sens(感,感觉)+itive(形容词后缀)→敏感的；索引p416

ex.en: But keeping sensitive information on these devices is increasingly a requirement of normal life.
ex.zh: 而在这些设备上保存敏感信息越来越成为日常生活的一种需求。

ex.en: Until this century, university libraries were not very price sensitive.
ex.zh: 直到本世纪，大学图书馆对（刊物的）售价都不是十分敏感。

ex.en: Some electronic instruments are so sensitive that they can detect temperature changes of a thousandth of a degree.
ex.zh: 有些电子仪器非常灵敏，能探测到千分之一度的温度变化。

ex.en: The instrument's sensitiveness allows researchers to detect extremely small changes in air temperature.
ex.zh: 该仪器的高灵敏度使研究人员能够探测到气温的极微小变化。

senses: n. 体贴,体谅;悟性;敏感性
n. （信息、话题等的）敏感性；体贴；过敏性；灵敏度；神经过敏；悟性

ex.en: Her sensitivity to students' worries made her the most trusted teacher in the school.
ex.zh: 她对学生的忧虑体贴入微，这使她成为全校最值得信赖的老师。

senses: n. [C] (探测光、热、压力等的)传感器，敏感元件
n. 传感器;敏感元件;探测设备
n. （探测光、热、压力等的）传感器，探测设备

ex.en: A sensor detects when the temperature falls and switches on the heating automatically.
ex.zh: 传感器探测到温度下降时会自动开启供暖。

ex.en: Modern cars contain dozens of sensors that monitor engine performance.
ex.zh: 现代汽车装有数十个监测发动机性能的传感器。

ex.en: The robot relies on pressure sensors to avoid damaging fragile objects.
ex.zh: 这款机器人依靠压力传感器来避免损坏易碎物品。

senses: adj. 知觉的,感觉的,感觉中枢的

ex.en: The study examines how sensory information from the environment is processed by the developing brain.
ex.zh: 该研究考察发育中的大脑如何处理来自环境的感官信息。

senses: a. 感官的；喜欢感官享受的
adj. 感官的,肉欲的,愉悦感官的,喜欢感官享受的,耽于肉欲的

ex.en: Critics praised the film's sensual imagery, noting how every scene appeals directly to the viewer's senses.
ex.zh: 评论家称赞影片诉诸感官的意象，指出每个画面都直接唤起观众的感官体验。

ex.en: The root sent, meaning to exist or be present, lies behind such everyday words as presence, essential and absentee.
ex.zh: 词根 sent 意为“存在”，是 presence、essential 和 absentee 等常用词的来源。

ex.en: Because senc and sent both mean to exist, they combine with prefixes to form words like absent, present and essence.
ex.zh: 由于 senc 与 sent 都表示“存在”，它们与前缀结合构成 absent、present 和 essence 等词。

ex.en: Consent, dissent and resent all contain the root sent or sens, which carries the basic meaning of feeling.
ex.zh: consent、dissent 和 resent 都包含词根 sent 或 sens，其基本含义是“感觉”。

ex.en: The judge reduced the prison sentence after the defendant showed genuine remorse and repaid the victims.
ex.zh: 被告真诚悔悟并赔偿受害者后，法官减轻了刑期。

senses: n. 情操,情感,情绪,多愁善感；意见,观点
sentiment.usage: 派生sentimental adj.情感的,情绪的;sentimentalist n.情感柔弱的人；n.观点，情绪；多愁善感，伤 感情绪；n.观点，看法，情绪；多愁善 感；索引p416

ex.en: At the next election none of the big parties seem likely to endorse this sentiment.
ex.zh: 在下一轮的选举中似乎没有一个大的政党认同这种观点。

ex.en: The speech reflected popular sentiment on immigration.
ex.zh: 这篇演讲反映了民众在移民问题上的情绪。

ex.en: There is growing sentiment in favour of reforming the tax system.
ex.zh: 支持改革税制的情绪日益高涨。

ex.en: He kept the old watch for sentimental reasons, although it had stopped working years before.
ex.zh: 他出于感情原因保留着那块旧手表，尽管它多年前就已停走。

senses: adj. ①分开的，分离的；单独的
separate.usage: 派生 separated adj. 分居的，分开的；separately adv. 分别地，单独地；separation n. 分离；分隔；(夫妻)分居；索引p416

ex.en: One reason why it is hard to design and teach such courses is that they cut across the insistence by top American universities that liberal-arts education and professional education should be kept separate, taught in different schools.
ex.zh: 这些课程难以开设和讲授的原因在于，它们有悖于美国一流大学一贯坚持的原则，即人文艺术教育与专业教育应保持分离，且分别由不同的院校来授课。

ex.en: The bedrooms are separate from the living area, which makes the flat feel larger.
ex.zh: 卧室与起居区分开，这使公寓显得更宽敞。

ex.en: The two issues, though related, should be kept separate in the discussion.
ex.zh: 这两个问题虽然相关，但在讨论中应分开处理。

ex.en: The two experiments were conducted separately so that neither group of participants could influence the other.
ex.zh: 两项实验分别进行，以便两组参与者互不影响。

ex.en: The separation of powers prevents any single branch of government from dominating the other two.
ex.zh: 权力分立可防止政府任何一个分支支配另外两个分支。

ex.en: Sept is the short form of September, the ninth month of the year, when many universities welcome their new students.
ex.zh: Sept 是 September（九月）的缩写，这个月许多大学迎来新生。

ex.en: Many universities admit new students in September, with a smaller second intake in January.
ex.zh: 许多大学在九月招收新生，一月还有较小规模的第二次入学。

ex.en: The Latin root sequ or secut, meaning to follow, appears in such common words as consequence, sequence and execute.
ex.zh: 拉丁词根 sequ 或 secut 意为“跟随”，出现在 consequence、sequence 和 execute 等常见词中。

senses: n. 一连串，一系列；顺序
n. 一系列，一连串；顺序，次序
sequence.usage: n.顺序，次序；一连串，一系列 v.按顺序排列；测定...序列；词根记忆：sequ(follow，跟随)+ence(表性质，状态)→一个跟一个→一连串；索引p416

ex.en: He had to attend a sequence of meetings.
ex.zh: 他得参加一系列会议。

ex.en: The genes are read in a precise sequence, and a single error can cause serious disease.
ex.zh: 基因按精确的顺序被读取，一个错误就可能引发严重的疾病。

ex.en: The film's opening sequence shows the city at dawn, empty and silent.
ex.zh: 影片的开场镜头展现了黎明时分空寂无声的城市。

ex.en: Words like series and serial contain the root seri, which suggests a chain or sequence of connected things.
ex.zh: series、serial 等词都包含词根 seri，表示一连串相互关联的事物。

senses: adj. 连续的；连续广播的，连载的；顺序排列的
n. 连载小说，连续电视；定期刊物(c)
serial.usage: 派生 serialize v. 连载或连播(某内容)；serialization n. 连载

ex.en: The newspaper published the novelist's latest story as a serial, printing one chapter every Sunday.
ex.zh: 报社将这位小说家的最新作品作为连载刊出，每周日刊登一章。

ex.en: The novel was published serially in a magazine before it appeared as a single volume.
ex.zh: 这部小说先在杂志上连载，随后才以单行本形式出版。

senses: n. 连续，一系列；系列节目
series.usage: 发音类似"serious(严重的)"→严重的事情(通常是祸)一发生就是一连串的→连续，一系列；另:a series of decisions一系列决定/a complex series of factors一系列复杂因素；索引p416

ex.en: Yet humans remain fascinated by the idea of robots that would look, move, and respond like humans, similar to those recently depicted on popular sci-fi TV series such as "Westworld" and "Humans".
ex.zh: 然而，人类仍然对机器人的想法着迷，机器人的外观、移动和响应都像人类，就像最近在流行的科幻电视连续剧《西部世界》和《人类》中描述的那样。

ex.en: A series of fires and overcrowded conditions led to the construction of the existing Treasury Building.
ex.zh: 一系列火灾和过度拥挤的环境导致了现有财政部大楼的修建。

ex.en: The company faced a series of lawsuits over the defective product.
ex.zh: 该公司因缺陷产品面临一连串诉讼。

senses: a. 稳重的；严肃的；严重的；重要的；认真的
serious.usage: 派生 seriousness n. 严肃，认真；严重性；seriously adv. 严肃地，认真地；严重地

ex.en: Doctors warned that the patient's condition was serious and that the operation could not be postponed.
ex.zh: 医生警告病人病情严重，手术不能再推迟。

senses: adv. 严重地；认真地；严肃地

ex.en: Health officials take the spread of the new virus seriously and have urged the public to remain calm.
ex.zh: 卫生官员高度重视新病毒的传播，并敦促公众保持冷静。

ex.en: The report emphasized the seriousness of climate change and called for immediate international cooperation.
ex.zh: 报告强调了气候变化的严重性，并呼吁立即开展国际合作。

senses: n. 布道,说教;(令人生厌的)冗长讲话

ex.en: The bishop's sermon on forgiveness moved many members of the congregation to tears.
ex.zh: 主教关于宽恕的布道令许多会众落泪。

ex.en: The root sert, meaning to join or put in, helps form verbs such as insert, assert and exert.
ex.zh: 词根 sert 意为“加入、插入”，构成了 insert、assert 和 exert 等动词。

ex.en: The root serv can mean to serve, as in service and servant, or to keep watch over, as in observe and conserve.
ex.zh: 词根 serv 既可表示“服务”，如 service 和 servant，也可表示“注视、保存”，如 observe 和 conserve。

ex.en: In reserve and preserve, the root serv or serve means to keep or hold back rather than to serve.
ex.zh: 在 reserve 和 preserve 中，词根 serv 或 serve 表示“保持、保留”，而非“服务”。

senses: n. 仆人,佣人,佣工;雇员;忠于某人(某事)的人

ex.en: In the nineteenth century, a single servant often had to cook, clean and care for the entire household.
ex.zh: 在十九世纪，一名仆人往往要为全家人做饭、打扫并照料日常起居。

senses: v. 接待(顾客)或为顾客取来(货物);有用,起作用
serve.usage: v.服务；提供，端上；接 待；词根记忆：serv(服务)+e→为（人、机构）服务；词根 serv=to serve 服务, to keep 保持；索引p416

ex.en: California's plan, which is expected to be finalized by the governor next year, should serve as a model.
ex.zh: 加利福尼亚州的计划有望在明年由州长最终敲定，它应该成为一个典范。

ex.en: He served as chairman of the committee for two terms.
ex.zh: 他担任该委员会主席两届。

ex.en: The new policy serves the interests of large corporations rather than small firms.
ex.zh: 新政策服务于大公司的利益，而非小企业。

senses: n. 服务,帮助;公共设施,公共事业
n. 维修,保养;行政部门,服务机构
n. 服务；国家政府部门
service.usage: 2019年阅读例：Small businesses and internet entrepreneurs are not well served at all by this decision. 这项裁决对小企业和互联网企业家们完全没有帮助；索引p416

ex.en: Google and Microsoft are among companies that already have these "single sign-on" systems that make it possible for users to log in just once but use many different services.
ex.zh: 许多公司都有"单次登录"系统，可使用户仅登录一次便可以享受多项不同服务，谷歌和微软正位列其中。

ex.en: The bank is famous for the quality of its customer service.
ex.zh: 这家银行以其客户服务的质量而闻名。

ex.en: The railway provides a regular service between the two cities.
ex.zh: 铁路在这两座城市之间提供定点班次服务。

senses: n. 会议,(一届)会议(c),一段时间
n. 一场，一节；会议；（法庭的）开庭；（议会等的）会议
session.usage: 发音类似“塞心”→一想到这周要开这么多的“会议”，我就感觉心塞→会议。

ex.en: We have both elementary and advanced training sessions.
ex.zh: 我们有初级和高级培训课程。

ex.en: Parliament will begin its autumn session next week.
ex.zh: 议会将于下周开始秋季会期。

ex.en: Each therapy session lasts about fifty minutes.
ex.zh: 每次治疗大约持续五十分钟。

senses: v. (set,set)放置;确定,决定;树立;校正,调整;落山,下沉
n. 一套,一副,一组;电气(或电子)器械
set.usage: set about着手;set aside留出,不顾;set off出发,激起;set up创立;set down写下;set forth阐明；小记：set sth./sb. back 使推迟，使延误；set in 到来，开始；set off 出发，起程；set out 出发，动身；set sth. out 安排，摆放

ex.en: The growth of higher education manifests itself in at least three quite different ways, and these in turn have given rise to different sets of problems.
ex.zh: 高等教育的发展至少表现在三种完全不同的方式上,而这些又产生不同的问题。

ex.en: If we set an end-of-quarter deadline, we'll never make it.
ex.zh: 如果我们设定的截止日期是季度末，那我们肯定完成不了。

ex.en: The committee will set new standards for food safety next year.
ex.zh: 委员会明年将制定新的食品安全标准。

setback.usage: 拓展记忆：和词组 set back（延误）一起记；索引p416

ex.en: The transition from school to work can be less of a setback if the start-up adult is ready for the move.
ex.zh: 如果这个准成年人做好了从学校向职场过渡的准备，那么在这一转变过程中就不会那么受挫了。

ex.en: The company suffered a major setback when its lead scientist resigned.
ex.zh: 首席科学家辞职后，公司遭受了重大挫折。

ex.en: Despite several early setbacks, the team eventually completed the research project.
ex.zh: 尽管早期屡遭挫折，团队最终还是完成了这项研究项目。

ex.en: The setter of the examination insisted that the questions reflected what students had actually been taught.
ex.zh: 试卷命题人坚称，试题反映了学生实际所学的内容。

setting.usage: 辨析:setting指事情发生或所处的环境、背景;environment指影响人的思想行为或事物发展的环境;surroundings指周围环境；n.环境；场景，背景；档位；设 置

ex.en: The study compares children's reading habits in the home setting and in the classroom.
ex.zh: 该研究比较了儿童在家庭和课堂环境中的阅读习惯。

senses: vi. 安定,安顿;停息,定居
v. 结束（争论、争端等）；定居；（最终）决定；使处于舒适的位置；（使）平静下来
settle.usage: set(往下)+tle→放下来不再漂泊即定居；问题放下来即解决；2019年阅读例：farm laborers are more likely to be settled rather than migrating 农场劳工更有可能定居而不是移民；索引p416

ex.en: She settled in Vienna after her father's death.
ex.zh: 在她的父亲死后，她就在维也纳定居了。

ex.en: While admitting that climate is a key element, Moritz notes that public debates have not settled yet.
ex.zh: 莫里茨虽然承认气候是一个关键因素，但他指出，公众的辩论还没有结束。

ex.en: The two companies agreed to settle the patent dispute out of court to avoid years of litigation.
ex.zh: 两家公司同意庭外和解这起专利纠纷，以免陷入旷日持久的诉讼。

senses: n. 定居地；解决；（解决纷争的）协议

ex.en: The management and unions have reached a settlement over new working conditions.
ex.zh: 资方和工会已就新的工作条件达成协议。

ex.en: At its peak around AD 600, this city was one of the largest human settlements in the world.
ex.zh: 在其鼎盛时期（公元600年左右），这座城市是世界上规模最大的人类定居地之一。

ex.en: After weeks of negotiation, the two companies finally reached a settlement.
ex.zh: 经过数周谈判，两家公司最终达成和解。

ex.en: The first settler families survived the harsh winters by learning farming methods from the native people.
ex.zh: 最早的移民家庭通过向原住民学习耕作方法，熬过了严酷的冬天。

ex.en: The study followed seven groups of volunteers for a full year to record changes in their sleeping habits.
ex.zh: 该研究对七组志愿者进行了整整一年的跟踪，记录他们睡眠习惯的变化。

ex.en: The government warned that it might sever diplomatic relations unless the two sides resumed negotiations.
ex.zh: 政府警告说，除非双方恢复谈判，否则可能断绝外交关系。

books.unit: 常见冠词、情态动词、系动词与限定词

ex.en: Several independent laboratories confirmed the results before the findings were published in a leading journal.
ex.zh: 几家独立实验室证实了这些结果，此后研究发现才发表在一家权威期刊上。

senses: adj. 十分严重的，极为恶劣的，严厉的；重的
adj. 十分严重的；严厉的；艰难的
severe.usage: 辨析:severe指坚持标准,不迁就;stern指严厉、严峻,毫不姑息;strict指精确严密；索引p416

ex.en: Even among those who got a cold, the ones who felt greater social support and received more frequent hugs had less severe symptoms.
ex.zh: 即使患上感冒,那些感受到更大社会支持且更频繁地得到拥抱的受试者也不会有太严重的症状。

ex.en: The fire has caused severe damage to the building.
ex.zh: 这场火灾给大楼造成了严重的损坏。

ex.en: In Indonesia, the program has provided enough food and medicine to substantially reduce severe growth problems among children.
ex.zh: 在印度尼西亚，该项目提供了足够的食物和药品，大大减少了儿童群体中的严重生长发育问题。
